To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

excitation-transcription (E-T) coupling in sympathetic neurons is initiated by a CaMKII-mediated decoding of the pattern of Ca(V) channel activation, which determines the strength of the signal that activates CREB.

the strength of excitation-transcription signaling depends on the membrane potential and is determined by Ca²+ channel gating rather than Ca²+ entry, and CaMKII links the activity of Ca²+ channels to activation of the transcription factor CREB.
the strength of excitation–transcription (ET) coupling is determined by the open probability (Po) of Ca(V) channel and that the CaMKII–CREB pathway is a key mediator of ET coupling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the electrical activity of a neuron is linked to the expression of specific genes in its nucleus.
the molecular mechanism of excitation-transcription (E-T) coupling in sympathetic neurons, and the role of Ca²+ in this process.
the mechanisms of excitation-transcription (e-T) coupling in sympathetic neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
excitation–transcription is a complex process that involves a number of steps and that it is regulated by a variety of signaling pathways.
the CaMKII-CREB pathway is a major component of excitation–transcription (E-T) coupling in neurons, and that CaMKII is a critical molecular sensor of the activity of voltage-gated calcium channels.
excitation-transcriptional coupling is a process in which a change in the electrical potential of a membrane is translated by a series of molecular interactions into a change in gene expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ca(V) channels, CaMKII, and CREB are a molecular mechanism of excitation-transcriptional coupling.
excitation–transcription (ETX) coupling in sympathetic neurons is mediated by CaMKII.

excitation-transcription (ET) coupling in sympathetic neurons is initiated by the activation of Ca²+ influx through Ca(V) channels, which is then transduced to the nucleus through a CaMKII-dependent signaling cascade.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Ca(V) channel open probability is a key factor in determining the strength of excitation- transcription coupling.

the strength of CaMKII signaling is a nonlinear function of membrane potential and Ca²+ influx, and that the molecular mechanism of excitation-transcription initiation is remarkably similar to that of excitation-secretion initiation.
excitation-contractions and excitation-secretions are not the only forms of excitation-coupled responses.
